utterance: Hi Samuel, I'm the doctor. I understand you've had tummy pain since last night. Can you tell me more about it — where exactly is the pain, and what does it feel like?
reply: Down here on the right side, low down. It started last night, about ten o'clock. So maybe fourteen hours. It is there all the time now. At first it sort of came and went. Maybe a seven out of ten.

awards.label: Whether the pain is constant or comes and goes

utterance: I see. Did the pain start somewhere else before settling on the right side — for example around your belly button?
reply: It actually started around my belly button. It moved down to the right sometime overnight.

awards.label: Red flag: Where the pain started and whether it has moved

utterance: Have you had any nausea or vomiting, and have you been able to eat or drink anything since it started?
reply: Felt sick since the early hours, and I threw up once this morning. I couldn't face breakfast. Not hungry at all, which isn't like me.

utterance: Have you had any fever, chills, or sweats?
reply: I felt hot and a bit shivery last night.

awards.label: Red flag: Fever, sweats or chills

utterance: Have your bowels been normal? Any diarrhoea or constipation since this started?
reply: No diarrhoea. I went normally yesterday morning, nothing since.

utterance: Any pain or burning when you pass urine, or needing to go more often?
Any pain in your testicles or groin, or any swelling there?
reply: No, nothing down there, and no lumps down there.

utterance: Have you ever had anything like this before, and have you had your appendix removed?
reply: Never had anything like this. Never had an operation, and I have still got my appendix as far as I know.

utterance: When did you last eat or drink anything, and what was it?
reply: No, just the usual. Mum's cooking on Sunday.

reply: No, I don't take any medicines.

awards.label: Refer to the emergency department today for surgical assessment

utterance:
Samuel, I'm concerned this is appendicitis — inflammation of your appendix, the small pouch attached to your bowel. Your story and my examination fit this very well: the pain that started around your belly button and moved to the lower right, the fever, feeling sick, and the tenderness when I pressed there.

This needs to be assessed in hospital today, because an inflamed appendix can burst and cause a serious infection. I'm sending you to the emergency department now. Please go straight there — don't wait at home, and don't eat or drink anything in case you need an operation or an anaesthetic.

If the pain suddenly gets much worse, or you feel faint, dizzy, or very unwell on the way, call 000 for an ambulance. Otherwise, have someone drive you, or go by ambulance if you're in too much pain to travel comfortably.
reply: Can I just go home and sleep it off instead?

utterance: I understand you'd rather go home, but I really don't recommend it. The signs point to appendicitis, and if it's left untreated the appendix can burst, which can make you very seriously unwell and need a bigger operation and a longer recovery. Going to hospital now, while it's still early, is the safest thing. It's important you go today, not wait.
reply: Right. I suppose I better go then.
